title: UNI-FLY awarded helicopter crew change contract for Baltica 2 offshore wind farm
summary: Under the contract, UNI-FLY will transport construction and commissioning personnel to and from one of the largest offshore wind projects under construction in the Baltic Sea.
body_markdown:
UNI-FLY, a provider of offshore helicopter services to the energy sector, today announced it has been awarded a contract to provide helicopter crew change support to the Baltica 2 offshore wind farm, currently under construction in the Polish sector of the Baltic Sea.


Under the contract, UNI-FLY will transport construction and commissioning personnel to and from the Baltica 2 site, one of the largest offshore wind projects under construction in the Baltic Sea.


The 1.5 GW wind farm is being developed by PGE Group and Ørsted and will consist of 107 turbines located approximately 40 km off the Polish coast, with commissioning planned for 2027.


To support the operation, UNI-FLY will establish a new operating base at Gdańsk Lech Wałęsa Airport, marking a significant expansion of its Baltic Sea presence and the company’s first base in Poland.


The base will serve as the hub for daily crew change flights and support flight operations, engineering, and ground support teams for the duration of the contract.


Operations commence with a Leonardo[AW169](https://helitrader.com/for-sale/helicopters/leonardo/aw169) helicopter, providing crew change services from day one of the contract. Capacity will be significantly boosted upon delivery of a new[AW139](https://helitrader.com/for-sale/helicopters/leonardo/aw139) in the seven-ton variant, which will expand payload and range, supporting heavier crew rotations and equipment transfers as construction activity on the wind farm scales up. The delivery will bring the company’s fleet to seven helicopters.


“We are proud to support PGE and Ørsted in delivering Baltica 2,” said Mads Bjerre Nielsen, CEO of UNI-FLY. “Our new Gdańsk Lech Wałęsa base and growing fleet mean we’ll be there for every rotation, safely and on schedule, from first flight to final turbine while supporting Poland’s energy transition.”


*This press release was prepared and distributed by UNI-FLY.*
